title: history
responsibility: Static guidance for Git-backed history, the pre-push hook and CI.

outputs.name: historyGuides
outputs.description: The exported array of the three static guides, in this order: 'history' covers Git-backed records, notes and the history index, 'hooks' covers the opt-in pre-push and commit-msg hooks, and 'ci' covers read-only CI verification and evidence publishing. Callers read this shared array when they need that guidance; it is an array literal evaluated once when the module loads and does not reflect the state of any repository.

examples.summary: CI verifies code without write access and publishes evidence from trusted code.
steps: harness-verify.yml runs the full check and verifies the exact commit, read-only.
It uploads the record and its evidence as an artifact, pass or fail.
harness-evidence.yml, on the default branch, validates that artifact and publishes it.
rules: The workflow that runs the code under test has contents: read and uses no secrets.
The publishing workflow never checks out, installs, builds or runs the verified commit. It validates the record as data: schema, seal, files, commit and tree.
External actions are pinned to full commit hashes; Bun and Rust are pinned versions.
Pushes to harness-evidence and to notes do not start a run.
Performance budgets are judged only against a baseline reviewed for that machine profile. A runner without one fails the budget gate. CI never establishes or approves a baseline.
Records of commits from other repositories are verified but not published.
antiPatterns: Do not use pull_request_target or give the verifying job a write token.
Do not let a workflow approve a budget.
exampleCommands: harness history attach --commit "$COMMIT" --record <record.json> # trusted CI artifact import
